Lessons.Title: Rewriting Quadratic Expressions in Factored Form (Part 4)
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: factor quadratic expressions with leading coefficient other than1 by regrouping a split middle term, verify signed coefficients and relate resulting factors to zeros. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition Unit 7 Lesson 10 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/7/10/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/7/10/index.html (CC BY 4.0). The source extends prior monic factoring to more complicated expressions.

Original quadratic 2x²+7x+3. Product of leading2 and constant3 equals6; find a split of middle coefficient7 into6+1. Then 2x²+6x+x+3=2x(x+3)+1(x+3)=(2x+1)(x+3). The zero candidates, if expression is set to0, are x−1/2 and x−3.

Original signed example 3x²−14x+8: product a·c=24 and split−14 as−12−2. Regroup 3x²−12x−2x+8=3x(x−4)−2(x−4)=(3x−2)(x−4), which gives zeros2/3 and4. Factoring is an identity; solving requires an additional equation equal zero.

Student task: construct two different grouping arrangements, expand to verify and explicitly distinguish factoring expression from solving equation. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 for suitable middle split, valid grouping, both full identities and clear domain/root interpretation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Leading coefficient
KeyConcepts.Definition: A nonmonic trinomial ax²+bx+c has a≠1.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Find factor products with a and c.

KeyConcepts.Title: Middle-term split
KeyConcepts.Definition: Search two numbers with sum b and product a·c for integer grouping.

KeyConcepts.Title: Grouping
KeyConcepts.Definition: Factor equal binomial from two pairs.

WorkedExamples.Title: Factor2x²+7x+3
WorkedExamples.Question: Use product a·c and sum b.
WorkedExamples.Method: Show distributive or equivalence-preserving algebra and independently verify every candidate solution.

WorkedExamples.Title: Factor with negative middle coefficient
WorkedExamples.Question: Factor3x²−14x+8.
WorkedExamples.Method: Show distributive or equivalence-preserving algebra and independently verify every candidate solution.

WorkedExamples.Title: Read roots when set to zero
WorkedExamples.Question: Solve(2x+1)(x+3)=0.
WorkedExamples.Method: Show distributive or equivalence-preserving algebra and independently verify every candidate solution.
WorkedExamples.Check: Factoring itself is not the same as solving until equation specified.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Forgetting to multiply a·c for nonmonic middle split
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Using c alone can choose wrong split.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Find product a·c and sum b.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Claiming factors automatically provide solutions when no equation is given
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: An expression has zeros but a solving problem needs equality.

SummaryPoints: Nonmonic factoring can be done by middle-term splitting and grouping.
Teacher reviews factor validity and root interpretation.
